hypothesis: Improve the scope and efficacy of laccase mediator system (LMS) treatment of perfluoroalkyl acids by a mechanistic investigation of each component, starting from literature reports of modest PFOA and PFOS losses over extended periods.
invalidators: a mass-balanced demonstration of PFOA or PFOS transformation products by any laccase mediator system
a Pleurotus ostreatus laccase preparation shown to degrade PFAAs with vessel and protein extraction accounted for
nextSteps: Use rigorous controls, in particular full mass balances including vessel and protein extraction, when evaluating bioinspired PFAS treatments.
Study PFAS-protein binding mechanisms as a route to bioinspired adsorptive materials, noting that the quantity of enzyme needed for adsorptive removal may be prohibitive.
openQuestions: Why did the earlier Pleurotus ostreatus laccase systems report PFOA and PFOS loss: sorption of the kind shown here, a property of that enzyme, or something else?
Which side chains of TvL bind PFOA after oxidation by the mediator?
outcomeSummary: While unable to replicate the oxidation of PFAAs, we show that interactions of the PFAA compounds with laccase and laccase mediator mixtures could cause an artifact that mimics transformation (<=60 %) of PFAAs. the LMS appears to be unable to detectably degrade the perfluorinated compounds PFOA and PFOS ... it is particularly important for researchers to use rigorous controls when analyzing treatment and removal strategies with novel bioinspired technologies

provenanceNotes: The positive control is a surrogate substrate (carbamazepine) run in a separate reactor set with the same enzyme, mediator and buffer, not an arm of the PFAA experiments. The ingest counts it as a designated positive control for the TvL/HBT findings and says so in each control's note; it does not count for the mediator screen, which used two other laccases.
The ingest treats the stated quantification range and the stated expected effect size as the sensitivity statement; the article reports no formal power analysis.

SI Tables S2 and S3 are images in the PDF; every cell was transcribed into curated/laccase/mass_balance.csv with the row and column as locator. The main text rounds them (82 % recovered becomes '18 +/- 2 % apparent loss').
The article has no author-contribution statement; every author is recorded with the role 'writing' only.
TvL/HBT against PFOS was tested only in the 0.1 uM 96 h and 24 h experiments; the two-week dosing experiment was PFOA only.
question: Can a laccase mediator system be optimised to degrade perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), as two earlier reports of modest losses suggested?

relations.note: PFOA removal >20 % at 10 days not replicated with TvL/HBT
PFOS removal not replicated with two commercial laccases and five mediators over 28 days

successCriteria: A statistically significant decrease in PFOA or PFOS mass, not only aqueous concentration, relative to untreated and enzyme-only controls, under conditions where the same enzyme and mediator transform a surrogate substrate.
title: Laccase mediator systems do not detectably degrade PFOA or PFOS; the reported loss is sorption to the enzyme
